# Evolution of a wastewater treatment plant challenges traditional design concepts

## Damian Domingueza,b, , Willi Gujera,b

aSwiss Federal Institute of Aquatic Science and Technology EAWAG, 8600 Du¨ bendorf, Switzerland bInstitute of Environmental Engineering, ETH Zurich 8093 Zurich, Switzerland

article info ABSTRACT

Article history: Traditional design and upgrade concepts for wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are Received 26 May 2005 based on the forecasting of load parameters over a period of 25–40 years. This approach is Received in revised form adequate as long as the environment of a WWTP is stable or predictable over this long time 13 January 2006 period. However, these conditions are usually not met, as the catchment area, discharge Accepted 23 January 2006 requirements, available technology and institutional conditions of a WWTP may change

drastically over time. The complexity and consequences of these dynamics are shown

Keywords: exemplarily in a case study analyzing the historical development of a plant from the initial Wastewater treatment planning steps to the current date. We conclude that the dynamics and complexity of the Design wastewater system makes reliable predictions impossible, and therefore question the Forecasting current design and upgrade approach. Instead, we propose to improve the planning and Uncertainty design of wastewater infrastructures through methodologies that systematically account Adaptive management for future uncertainty, like, e.g. scenario planning.
